query_text: what is a good title for a poem I'm writing about a religious boy who has been sheltered from the outside world by his family, but one day he leaves his house and sees the reality of the world?

content.text:
Here are some title ideas for your poem, each capturing a different tone or angle of the theme:

1. **"Beyond the Garden Wall"** – Suggests a paradise-like shelter being left behind, with religious undertones.
2. **"First Light"** – Implies seeing the world clearly and truthfully for the very first time.
3. **"The Unveiled World"** – Suggests the lifting of a veil, both literally and spiritually.
4. **"Outside the Sanctuary"** – Directly references the religious safety of home versus the rawness of the outside world.
5. **"Crossing the Threshold"** – A powerful metaphor for leaving one world and entering another.
6. **"The Fall from Grace"** – A biblical reference suggesting the loss of innocence upon seeing reality.
7. **"Barefoot on Common Ground"** – Implies stepping into the real world, unprotected and exposed for the first time.
8. **"Among the Sinners"** – Reflects how the boy might perceive the outside world through his religious lens.
9. **"Where God Doesn't Reach"** – A provocative title suggesting places beyond the boy's sheltered faith.
10. **"Stained Glass Eyes"** – Metaphor for seeing the world through a filtered, religious perspective, like light through a church window.
11. **"The World Without Scripture"** – Implies a life and world that exists outside of his religious upbringing.
12. **"Beyond the Amen"** – Suggests stepping into the unknown world that exists past the boundaries of prayer.

My personal favorite for your poem would be **"Stained Glass Eyes"** — it's poetic, layered with religious imagery, and perfectly captures the idea of a boy whose entire perception of the world has been shaped by his sheltered, faith-based upbringing. It's both beautiful and thought-provoking!
